subject: Inconsistent results of the Besag model between different formats of same formula

messages.author: 13b95c7a86073d8e
messages.subject: Inconsistent results of the Besag model between different formats of same formula
parts:
Hi all,

I am learning how to build the Besag model using the INLA.  First, I noted some differences in the output of the same model (code and data) between two different computers, but the difference is at decimal places, which is negligible to me.  Recently I have found that the outputs were rather different between the following formats of the same formula.  The only difference is using "=" or "<-" to specify the same formula, or putting the formula inside a pair of parenthesis as below (f1-f3).  Additionally, I did not understand why the formula f4 using "graph = g gave different result from using graph="bbsquail2.graph", with the g being specified as "g="bbsquail2.graph" in the code I attached in this message.  I attached my test code, data, and graph file.  I greatly appreciate it if you could help me find whether it is my code is wrong, or my model is incorrect, or it is because the R version and INLA version are incompatible. 

f1= count ~ f(inla.group(inp3yr$crppland),model="rw2",hyper=prior.rw2, 
   replicate=yr.id2)+f(key, model="besag",graph="bbsquail2.graph",
   hyper=prior.car, replicate=yr.id)+f(key2,model="iid")

f2 <- count ~ f(inla.group(inp3yr$crppland),model="rw2",hyper=prior.rw2, 
   replicate=yr.id2)+f(key, model="besag",graph="bbsquail2.graph",
   hyper=prior.car, replicate=yr.id)+f(key2,model="iid")

f3<-(count ~ f(inla.group(inp3yr$crppland),model="rw2",hyper=prior.rw2, 
   replicate=yr.id2)+f(key, model="besag",graph="bbsquail2.graph",
   hyper=prior.car, replicate=yr.id)+f(key2,model="iid"))

f4= count ~ f(inla.group(inp3yr$crppland),model="rw2",hyper=prior.rw2, 
   replicate=yr.id2)+f(key, model="besag",graph=g,
   hyper=prior.car, replicate=yr.id)+f(key2,model="iid")

The DIC outputs from the INLA _17.06.20 under the R 3.3.2, on a Dell Latitude E6540, were
> r1$dic$dic
[1] 6119.315
> r2$dic$dic
[1] 6119.315
> r3$dic$dic
[1] 6119.315
> r4$dic$dic
[1] 5908.395
> 

Although the r1-r3 had the same DIC under the running environments, they (r1-r3) were rather different from each other on another computer.  If you can r4 had different DIC from r1-r3.

Many thanks in advance!

Guiming

On 11/08/2017 10:15, Guiming Wang wrote:
> count ~ f(inla.group(inp3yr$crppland),model="rw2",hyper=prior.rw2,
> replicate=yr.id2)+f(key, model="besag",graph="bbsquail2.graph",
> hyper=prior.car, replicate=yr.id)+f(key2,model="iid")

For me sounds that the model is not suitable for the data. You may had
warnings about negative eigenvalues. One way to check if you can trust a
result is to look at the corrected standard deviation for the
hyperparameters. One of your cases I had:

> grep('corrected stdev', r1$logfile, value=TRUE)
[1] "Compute corrected stdev for theta[0]: negative 1.000000 positive
2.480853"
[2] "Compute corrected stdev for theta[1]: negative 6.721561 positive
10.651360"
[3] "Compute corrected stdev for theta[2]: negative 1.000000 positive
1.065002"
[4] "Compute corrected stdev for theta[3]: negative 5.959927 positive
6.530845"

which is not good because there are ones far from 1.

Going back to your model I see that you have structured effect
replicated + iid by the same index, however not replicated. Then you
have a zero inflated likelihood type 1. I tried 'poisson'
and it gives no problems, as you can see bellow:

r1p = inla(f1,family="poisson",data=inp3yr,
control.compute=list(dic=TRUE, waic=TRUE, cpo=TRUE))

r2p = inla(f2,family="poisson",data=inp3yr,
control.compute=list(dic=TRUE, waic=TRUE, cpo=TRUE))

r3p = inla(f3,family="poisson",data=inp3yr,

r4p = inla(f4,family="poisson",data=inp3yr,

messages.author: 66ed4f72a898a51c
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Inconsistent results of the Besag model between different formats of same formula
parts:
> or my model is incorrect
I have two suggestions:

1. use the scaled version of the intrinsic 'rw2' effect (see
http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2211675313000407) and
a penalized complexity prior for its precision (see
http://projecteuclid.org/euclid.ss/1491465621)

2. instead of having 'besag' replicated + 'iid' not replicated, you can
have a bit more flexible one replicating a 'bym' model. However, use
'bym2' because it has a nicer interpretation, as you can see in
http://journals.sagepub.com/doi/pdf/10.1177/0962280216660421

### code suggestion
pcprec <- list(prec=list(prior="pcprec", params=c(1, 0.01)))
ff <- count ~ f(inla.group(crppland), model="rw2",
scale.model=TRUE, hyper=pcprec, replicate=yr.id2) +
f(key, model="bym2", graph="bbsquail2.graph", replicate=yr.id)
rr <- inla(ff, family="poisson", data=inp3yr,
control.compute=list(dic=TRUE, waic=TRUE, cpo=TRUE))

Elias

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Inconsistent results of the Besag model between different formats of same formula
parts:
On 11/08/2017 12:09, Guiming Wang wrote:
> Thanks. I will redo the models following your suggestions. About the
> Poisson distributions, the response variable count has quite a few
> zero. This is why I used the ZIP. Do you think a negative binomial
> distribution will work too?

Usually one uses ZIP it has **more** zeros than the expected for the
Poisson. The negative binomial is a Poisson with Gamma iid effect and so
it may be confounded wit the Gaussian iid effect you already had.
Elias
